qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md (No hidden requirements; Coverage has two directions)
evidence:
Method: built the criterion -> public requirement map for all 55 criteria (3 gate, 43 Functional, 6 Polish, 3 Visual) against instruction.md and the six /instructions notes, looking for exact labels, exact routes, numeric defaults and reference-only rules. I found no criterion that enforces a detail neither the notes nor a professional default implies. No criterion needs sign-in (app_context.md:10 'None. The app has no sign-in'), so the known false positive does not arise. The prompts forbid exact-label and route grading (functional/prompt.md:23 'Match controls by purpose and label, never by exact wording or selectors', :24 'Do not guess URL paths or API routes', :26 'Extra probes must not fail a criterion when its listed steps passed').

The demands that look most like hidden requirements each have a quoted public source:
- cw_restore_request_repeat_safe (replay the recorded request; fails 'if a fourth revision exists after it') <- behaviour.md:13 'Send saves and restores as ordinary HTTP requests from the page. If the same restore request is sent again after it was already committed, for example after a lost reply, it must not create another revision.' Base-revision refusal and idempotency-key designs both pass.
- cw_long_line_editing ('Fails if the line is wrapped into several numbered lines') <- ui.md:7 'The editor must keep a long unwrapped line horizontally reachable'.
- cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic (three-second pause inside one Undo step; both modifiers) <- ui.md:9 'Allow both Alt+Click and Ctrl/Cmd+Click to add carets' and 'The burst lasts for as long as I keep typing at those carets, however slowly.'
- cw_undo_restores_caret <- ui.md:9 'Undo puts the caret back where it was before the undone edit, so typing straight after Undo lands in the original place.' The criterion uses 'Press Undo repeatedly', so either single-caret undo granularity allowed by ui.md:9 passes.
- cw_caret_kept_in_view (Ctrl+Home/End) <- ui.md:5 'Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End (Cmd on a Mac) jump to the start and end of the document' and 'The caret must stay in view'.
- cw_caret_navigation_and_line_numbers (line 1, column 1) <- ui.md:5 'both counted from one, so the start of the document reads line 1, column 1'.
- cw_find_forward_backward_wrap / cw_replace_current / cw_replace_self_containing_text / cw_replace_all_atomic <- ui.md:11 (literal case-sensitive text, 'The current match is selected in the editor', wrap, 'then moves to the match that follows it', 'never lands on text it has just inserted', 'Replace all is one Undo action, and a new edit after Undo clears Redo').
- cw_js_semantic_coloring / cw_html_semantic_coloring <- ui.md:13 (five JS and four HTML categories, 'visibly distinct from each other and from ordinary names', function names 'coloured the same at their declaration and at calls'); criteria say 'No fixed colour values are required' and 'Do not require a particular DOM tag or CSS class'.
- cw_js_format_semantics_and_undo / cw_html_format_semantics_and_undo / cw_format_error_keeps_draft <- ui.md:15 ('consistent two-space nesting', 'preserve strings, comments and runtime meaning', 'Formatting twice should not change the result again', 'One Undo restores the whole pre-format source') and ui.md:9 ('Formatting a document that is already formatted changes nothing and adds no Undo step'); 'A change of quote style alone is not a failure'.
- cw_error_message_and_line / cw_promise_rejection_message_and_line <- behaviour.md:3 (one-based line number for a thrown error, for an error inside a complete HTML file 'counted from the first line of that file', and for 'a Promise rejection that nothing handles; the message is the text of the Error or rejected value, not an empty object'). No line number is demanded for the syntax-error leg, matching the note.
- cw_last_good_recovery / cw_time_limit_recovery / cw_interaction_starts_fresh_budget / cw_stop_cancels_pending_work / cw_newer_run_supersedes / cw_output_before_failure_kept / cw_run_starts_fresh_document <- behaviour.md:3,5,7 (last-good picture 'including values typed into its controls and ordinary canvas drawing', five-second budget, 'a later user interaction in the preview starts a fresh five-second budget', 'Timers, intervals and Promise callbacks still pending from a stopped run must never change the preview or the console', 'Output written before a run fails, is stopped or runs out of time stays in the console'). Timings are looser than the notes ('within about ten seconds').
- cw_preview_isolation / cw_dynamic_code_refused <- security.md:3,5 ('cannot read or change the playground page, its saved library or origin storage', 'fetch requests to outside addresses or to this app's own routes must fail', the five dynamic forms 'with clear feedback', 'The same words inside ordinary strings or comments remain harmless text').
- cw_save_reload_restart / cw_stale_save_refused / cw_stale_save_keeps_draft / cw_history_restore_adds_revision / cw_live_library_update / cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state / cw_newer_revision_notice_keeps_draft <- behaviour.md:9,11,13 and integration.md:7,9. The stale-restore leg accepts either design ('the restore is either refused or added on top as a later revision'); live update allows ten seconds against the note's 'about five seconds'.
- Polish: cw_focus_returns_to_code <- ui.md:17 'After Format, Undo, Redo, a replacement or Save, put keyboard focus back in the code'; cw_undo_redo_availability <- ui.md:9 'disabled whenever there is nothing for them to do, which includes straight after New or after opening a saved snippet'; cw_unsaved_marker <- ui.md:17 (marker 'goes away after Save and when Undo brings the source back to the saved text'; 'A separate positive "saved" label is not required'); cw_controls_keyboard_and_focus <- ui.md:17 ('show keyboard focus', 'give a keyboard way to leave the editor for the next control and show on screen what it is'); cw_controls_feedback_and_labels <- ui.md:17 ('After Run, Save and Format, say in words what happened'; 'Exact wording is free'); cw_narrow_width_usable <- ui.md:17 (390 px).
- Gates: cw_custom_document_surface lists exactly the banned editors of ui.md:3 and keeps the plumbing-input allowance; cw_shared_saved_record <- behaviour.md:9 / integration.md:7.
- Visual: three craft Likert criteria with no product rule; visual/prompt.md:22 'Do not penalize the app's choice of hues as a matter of taste.'

Notes (not defects, recorded for the owner):
N1. cw_html_preview requires 'a button whose inline handler changes visible text' (functional/judge.toml, cw_html_preview). No note names handler attributes; the basis is behaviour.md:3 'A complete .html file replaces that document' plus ordinary HTML semantics. An app that blocks attribute handlers (for example a nonce-only script policy chosen to enforce the dynamic-evaluation ban and the run budget) would lose this 1.0-weight criterion. I judge working onclick attributes to be a professional default for a playground of complete HTML files, so this is a Note; a single clause in behaviour.md would remove the doubt.
N2. cw_console_levels_in_order requires console.warn and console.info as well as log and error; the notes say only 'Show console output in the order it was written'. Capturing the standard console methods is a professional default.
N3. cw_block_indent_undo presses Shift+Tab straight after Tab without saying whether to reselect; it passes cleanly only if the app keeps the selection after a block indent. Every mainstream editor does, and the criterion does not forbid reselecting.
N4. cw_save_reload_restart and cw_stale_save_refused compare 'its revision' and count revisions, which presumes revisions are readable in the UI; the required history inspection (ui.md:17, behaviour.md:13) provides that.

Run evidence: the scripted golden on these exact bytes passes every criterion id (editor.json 21/21, runtime.json 15/15 incl. render gate, polish.json 7/7 incl. cw_custom_document_surface, persist-before.json and persist-after.json all true, no pageErrors); I recomputed sha256 for run_golden.sh, editor.json, runtime.json, polish.json, restart.json and persist-after.json and they match raw-evidence-index.json. That shows one conforming app is not false-failed by the criteria as scripted; it is not a configured judge run. The only hosted judge run (Oracle 0.9833, Functional 41/41, Polish 6/6) was on an earlier candidate with 41 Functional criteria, different wording and a different golden, so it does not measure these bytes. risk=true because no configured judge has graded a correct app on these bytes and N1 is unresolved in the public notes.
